headline: Microsoft’s open-source SkillOpt automatically upgrades AI agent skills without touching model weights
summary: SkillOpt uses deep-learning-style optimization to evolve agent skill documents based on performance feedback, significantly boosting accuracy for models like GPT-5.5 and Qwen on industry benchmarks.
details: Microsoft has released SkillOpt, a new open-source (MIT Licensed) framework designed to automatically optimize AI agent skills. This innovative tool allows AI models to adapt to specific enterprise use cases and complex workflows without altering the underlying model's weights.

Previously, optimizing these agent skills was a slow and error-prone manual process. Users had to retype instructions in text-based markdown files, essentially playing a 'guessing game' to find changes that might improve performance and reduce errors.

SkillOpt introduces an optimizer that treats the agent's skill document as a trainable object, allowing it to evolve based on performance feedback. It employs deep-learning-style optimization to systematically explore modifications to the document.

On various industry benchmarks, SkillOpt has demonstrated superior performance, significantly outperforming existing baselines. It has boosted the accuracy of frontier models such as GPT-5.5 and Qwen, creating compact and transferable skill artifacts.

Agent skills are crucial for packaging procedural knowledge, including domain heuristics and tool-use policies, into natural-language specifications. They provide an external interface for agents to adapt to complex enterprise workflows without modifying the core AI model.

A key challenge in previous methods was the lack of mathematical discipline in updating skill documents, leading to volatility. Microsoft's Yifan Yang noted issues like no step-size control, lack of validation, and no negative memory, which could quietly regress performance.

SkillOpt addresses these failure modes by applying deep-learning-style controls, such as learning rates, validation gates, and momentum. This ensures that changes made to the skill document are mathematically sound and reliably lead to improvements.

The framework optimizes a text document through an iterative propose-and-test loop. This process separates the model executing the tasks from the model responsible for optimizing the skill, ensuring a robust and controlled evolution of agent capabilities.

headline_marked: [[Elon Musk posts anti-immigrant content]] amid Belfast riots, ahead of SpaceX IPO
headline: Elon Musk posts anti-immigrant content amid Belfast riots, ahead of SpaceX IPO
summary: Elon Musk's posts on X, supporting hard-right views and calling for protests, coincide with violence in Belfast and SpaceX's upcoming stock market debut. His statements are listed as a risk factor in SpaceX's IPO filings.
details: Elon Musk has posted a wave of anti-immigrant content on X, coinciding with ongoing riots in Belfast, Northern Ireland. These actions come as his company SpaceX prepares for its stock market debut later this week.

Following a knife attack in Belfast, Musk declared support for the hard-right political party Restore Britain. He reposted statements from party leader Rupert Lowe advocating for large-scale migrant deportation and prosecuting officials who 'knowingly placed dangerous third world savages in our communities,' adding 'This is the way.'

Musk also shared a list of protest locations in Belfast, encouraging followers to protest 'REPEATEDLY and LOUDLY' for change. He reposted a mocking take on the idea that 'You can’t solve problems with violence.'

The suspected attacker in Belfast is a Sudanese refugee legally residing in the UK, according to The New York Times. Rioters subsequently gathered, setting vehicles and homes ablaze, primarily in immigrant communities, and threw objects at police.

Musk's anti-immigrant posts are part of a pattern of controversial rhetoric on his X account. He previously called for the execution of Iraqi suspects in a German rape trial and responded to 'you can’t teach savages not to rape' with 'Murderous migrants must go.'

UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer condemned the violence in Belfast and acknowledged the role of social media in encouraging it. Ofcom, the UK's communications regulator, warned online platforms about their obligation to remove illegal content under the Online Safety Act.

Ofcom's group director for online safety, Oliver Griffiths, noted that civil unrest in Belfast, including racially motivated violence and arson, appeared to have been incited online. This highlights the platforms' responsibility in managing such content.

Musk responded to accusations by stating, 'Murderous migrants beheading innocent people in their home town is what’s making people angry, not ‘social media’!' He has previously expressed fears that white people will go 'extinct.'
